The code snippet provided is a method `singularFieldToProtoValue` which converts various types of values into their corresponding protocol buffer values. The method handles different types of `schemaInformation.getType()` and for each type, it checks the type of `value` and converts it accordingly. In the case of `TIMESTAMP`, the method attempts to parse a `String` value into an `Instant` using `Instant.from`. The `from` method, as per the API documentation, may throw a `DateTimeException` if it is unable to convert the provided `temporal` object to an `Instant`.

The method `singularFieldToProtoValue` includes a try-catch block to handle `DateTimeParseException` when parsing the `String` value to `Instant` using `DateTimeFormatter.ISO_DATE_TIME`. If this fails, it tries to parse the `String` value as a long and then as an `Instant` using `DATETIME_SPACE_FORMATTER`. However, the `DateTimeException` from `Instant.from` is not explicitly caught. This means that if the `temporal` object (in this case, the result of `DateTimeFormatter.ISO_DATE_TIME.parse` or `DATETIME_SPACE_FORMATTER.parse`) is not a valid `Instant`, a `DateTimeException` will be thrown and not caught by the current exception handling mechanism. Therefore, the `DateTimeException` is not avoided in this context.
remark: The `DateTimeException` will be thrown if the `temporal` object, which is the result of parsing the `String` value, is not a valid `Instant`. This can happen if the `String` value cannot be parsed using either `DateTimeFormatter.ISO_DATE_TIME` or `DATETIME_SPACE_FORMATTER`, or if the parsed `temporal` object does not contain the necessary fields to create an `Instant` (i.e., `INSTANT_SECONDS` and `NANO_OF_SECOND`).
